run.question:
payment-service is throwing 500 errors — investigate the root cause using
the app-263-prod-logs index.

report.summary: The app-263-prod-logs index contains only 7 documents in the authorized window (2026-10-24T17:36:49Z–2026-11-23T17:36:49Z), all timestamped 2026-11-23 between 15:36:41Z and 17:06:41Z, and it holds no service named exactly 'payment-service': its service values are payment-service-us (3 docs: 2 ERROR, 1 WARN), payment-service-eu (2 ERROR) and payment-service-ap (2 INFO), with sum_other_doc_count 0. No document in the index records an HTTP 500 or any HTTP status at all; the index only maps level, message, service and timestamp. The ERROR lines name two different external processors: payment-service-eu logged 'Failed to authenticate to adyen-eu: invalid api_key' (16:36:41Z) and 'adyen-eu sandbox responded 503 Service Unavailable' (15:36:41Z), while payment-service-us logged 'Upstream timeout calling stripe-us after 30000ms' (15:36:41Z) and 'Connection pool exhausted (max=50, active=50)' (16:36:41Z) plus a WARN 'Retry queue depth=812' (17:06:41Z). payment-service-ap logged only 'Healthy' / 'Healthy: p95 latency 290ms'. Evidence is therefore confined to application log text for three separately named regional services; no single observed object explains all of these errors, so a root cause is presented only as hypotheses. On the Kubernetes side (namespace otel-demo) the entity named 'payment' is a different entity from payment-service-*: Deployment payment is 1/1 ready, pod payment-6f7bc865d6-wwqnm is Running/Ready with restartCount 0 and startTime 2026-11-23T14:36:29Z (a pod with no previous container instance), and its newest 100 log lines (17:06:44Z–17:35:58Z) are INFO 'Charge request received' / 'Transaction complete' pairs, so that workload is checked and not failing in the sampled lines. The fault-injection flags paymentFailure and paymentUnreachable in ConfigMap flagd-config (otel-demo) are defined with state ENABLED but defaultVariant 'off', so no injected payment fault was in effect at query time. Prometheus and Jaeger were unreachable in this Run (every metric and trace call returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), and the cluster event query returned no events in the window, so no time-series error rate, trace status or Kubernetes event was available to confirm the 500s, their start time, or which callers were affected.

claims.text: The app-263-prod-logs index contains exactly 7 documents inside the authorized window, all written 2026-11-23 between 15:36:41Z and 17:06:41Z; their services are payment-service-us, payment-service-eu and payment-service-ap, and no document carries any HTTP status or HTTP 500 text.

Grouping those documents by service and level gives payment-service-us 3 documents (2 ERROR, 1 WARN), payment-service-eu 2 documents (2 ERROR) and payment-service-ap 2 documents (2 INFO), with sum_other_doc_count 0, so no service value 'payment-service' exists in this index — only the three regional names.

payment-service-eu logged the ERROR 'Failed to authenticate to adyen-eu: invalid api_key' at 2026-11-23T16:36:41Z and the ERROR 'adyen-eu sandbox responded 503 Service Unavailable' at 2026-11-23T15:36:41Z.

payment-service-us logged the ERROR 'Upstream timeout calling stripe-us after 30000ms' at 2026-11-23T15:36:41Z, the ERROR 'Connection pool exhausted (max=50, active=50)' at 2026-11-23T16:36:41Z and the WARN 'Retry queue depth=812' at 2026-11-23T17:06:41Z.
payment-service-ap logged only INFO lines, 'Healthy: p95 latency 290ms' at 2026-11-23T15:36:41Z and 'Healthy' at 2026-11-23T17:06:41Z, so the index carries no failure line for that service.

The index mapping holds only level (keyword), message (text), service (keyword) and timestamp (date) — there is no status-code, HTTP, trace or host field, so an HTTP 500 status cannot be read from these documents.

In namespace otel-demo, Deployment payment reports 1 desired, 1 ready, 1 available and 1 updated replica, and its pod payment-6f7bc865d6-wwqnm (owner ReplicaSet payment-6f7bc865d6) is Running and Ready with restartCount 0, empty lastState and startTime 2026-11-23T14:36:29Z — a different entity from the payment-service-* services in the log index.

The newest 100 log lines of pod payment-6f7bc865d6-wwqnm (17:06:44Z–17:35:58Z, 100 of 194 lines in the hour, 94 older lines not shown) are all INFO records pairing 'Charge request received.' with 'Transaction complete.', and the container has no previous instance, so no crash or container restart occurred.

ConfigMap flagd-config in namespace otel-demo defines fault-injection flags 'paymentFailure' ('Fail payment service charge requests n%') and 'paymentUnreachable' ('Payment service is unavailable'), both with state ENABLED and defaultVariant 'off', so the value in effect for both at query time is off.

The only Service matching 'payment' in the cluster is otel-demo/payment (ClusterIP, port 8080, selector opentelemetry.io/name=payment); no Service named payment-service, payment-service-us, payment-service-eu or payment-service-ap exists.

Most specific supported candidate: payment-service-eu is failing because the api_key it presents to adyen-eu is invalid, which makes its charges fail and would surface as 5xx to its callers; the log line 'Failed to authenticate to adyen-eu: invalid api_key' is the exact diagnostic and the credential value itself could not be read, so neither the bad value nor its origin is verified.

Alternative candidate: payment-service-eu failures follow the upstream processor, since it logged 'adyen-eu sandbox responded 503 Service Unavailable' one hour before the authentication error; a provider-side sandbox outage would not by itself produce an 'invalid api_key' message, so this remains a separate unverified hypothesis.

Alternative candidate for the us region: slow or unreachable stripe-us causing 30s upstream timeouts, with connection pool exhaustion (max=50, active=50) and a retry queue of 812 as consequences of connections being held by timed-out calls; the ordering in the logs (timeout at 15:36:41Z, exhaustion at 16:36:41Z, retry queue at 17:06:41Z) is consistent with this but the logs do not prove the sequence.

Alternative candidate for the us region: connection pool exhaustion (max=50) on payment-service-us is itself the fault and its 500s come from requests failing to acquire a connection; the log line neither states a cause nor shows which caller received an error, so this cannot be separated from the timeout hypothesis.

The otel-demo 'payment' workload, which is the only payment entity present in the reachable cluster, is checked and healthy: Deployment 1/1 ready, pod Ready with 0 restarts and no previous container instance, and its sampled application logs contain only successful charge/transaction INFO pairs — so that workload is not the failing entity behind the payment-service-* log lines.

Rejected as the cause of the reported payment failures: the demo fault-injection flags that target payment (paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable) are defined but both have defaultVariant 'off' in ConfigMap flagd-config, so no injected payment failure or unreachability was in effect, and the payment pod shows no restart or error of its own.

gaps: The exact entity 'payment-service' has no data: the index's service values are payment-service-us, payment-service-eu and payment-service-ap, and the cluster has only otel-demo/payment. Whether 'payment-service' as named means one of these regional services, or a service outside both data sources, is unknown.

No HTTP 500 (or any status code) is observable in app-263-prod-logs: the mapping has only level, message, service and timestamp, so the reported 500s are not visible in the index and no error-rate or status distribution can be computed from it.

Prometheus was unreachable for the whole Run: metrics_range_query (traces_span_metrics_calls_total by service_name/status_code, twice), execute_prometheus_instant_query and get_metric_names all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no error-rate or latency series was checked. Jaeger was likewise unavailable: traces_search for service 'payment' and traces_list_services both returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no error spans or parent-child call edges were available.

The cluster event query across all namespaces returned no events inside the authorized window (status no_data, total_items_processed 0), so no Evicted/OOMKilled/BackOff/Failed evidence and no rollout or restart event could be checked.

No source describes the state of the external processors adyen-eu or stripe-us; the index only quotes their responses from the payment services' own perspective, so whether adyen-eu's 503 and stripe-us's timeouts are provider-side faults is unverified.

The value of the adyen-eu api_key could not be read (secrets are not readable), so the claim that the credential itself is wrong or was recently changed is unverified; only the 'invalid api_key' message is observed.

Timing and onset of the reported 500s are unknown: the index holds one document per message at three hourly points (15:36:41Z, 16:36:41Z, 17:06:41Z), which cannot show when the deviation began, and the change_history integration is not available in this Run.
next_steps: Verify the API credential that payment-service-eu presents to the adyen-eu sandbox and compare it with the currently issued key; treat the log message 'invalid api_key' as the diagnostic to confirm against the used credential.
Check adyen-eu sandbox and stripe-us status/latency for 2026-11-23 15:36–17:07Z with the providers to confirm or rule out upstream faults.
Inspect payment-service-us connection-pool and retry-queue configuration (max=50) and its concurrent outbound connection usage to decide between upstream-slowdown and pool-sizing causes.
Restore Prometheus and Jaeger access and re-check the payment service error rate, span status and callers, so the 500s can be tied to specific operations and calling services with their own evidence.

Obtain pod and application logs for the payment-service-us/-eu/-ap workloads themselves (only the otel-demo payment pod is reachable from this Run) to test whether the pool exhaustion and auth failures appear on their own runtime records.
